title: Travel Problems
summary: A traveller explains a missed connection at the airport and asks for help rebooking the next flight.
description: An intermediate conversation at an airline counter. Focuses on polite complaints, conditional language ('if…then…'), and useful travel vocabulary (layover, connection, rebook).

vocabulary.definition: arriving or happening later than planned
a flight that you take after another to continue your journey
to arrive too late for something, like a flight or a bus
to arrange a new ticket or reservation
a short stay between flights, usually in another city

dialogue.text: Good afternoon. How can I help you?
Good afternoon. My flight from Madrid was delayed, and I missed my connection.
I am sorry to hear that. May I see your boarding pass?
Here you are. I was supposed to fly to Boston at four, but my layover was only forty minutes.
I see. The next flight to Boston leaves at eight this evening. Would you like to rebook?
If there is a seat available, yes, please. Otherwise, I will need a hotel for the night.
There is a seat. I will put you on the eight o'clock flight. You will still make your meeting tomorrow morning.
That is great. Thank you very much for your help.
You are welcome. Here is your new boarding pass. Safe travels.

questions.q: Why did the traveller miss the connection?
options: They arrived late at the airport

questions.q: What was the length of the original layover?

options: A new flight at eight p.m.

trueFalse.statement: The traveller is flying to Boston.
trueFalse.explanation: The traveller says 'I was supposed to fly to Boston at four.'

trueFalse.statement: The traveller will have to spend the night in a hotel.
trueFalse.explanation: The agent finds a seat on the eight o'clock flight, so the traveller will still make the meeting the next morning.

teacherTips: Pre-teach the conditional structure 'If there is… then I will…' — a key phrase for real-life problem-solving.
After listening, students discuss in pairs: 'Have you ever missed a flight? What did you do?'
Extension: learners role-play a complaint at a hotel reception or a shop using the same polite structures.

es.title: Problemas de viaje
es.summary: Un viajero explica una conexión perdida en el aeropuerto y pide ayuda para reservar el siguiente vuelo.
es.description: Una conversación intermedia en el mostrador de una aerolínea. Se centra en quejas educadas, lenguaje condicional ('if…then…') y vocabulario útil de viaje (layover, connection, rebook).

vocabulary.definition: que llega o sucede más tarde de lo planeado
un vuelo que tomas después de otro para continuar el viaje
llegar demasiado tarde para algo, como un vuelo o un autobús
conseguir un nuevo billete o reserva
una estancia corta entre vuelos, normalmente en otra ciudad

questions.q: ¿Por qué perdió la conexión el viajero?

options: Un nuevo vuelo a las ocho de la tarde

trueFalse.explanation: El viajero dice 'I was supposed to fly to Boston at four'.

trueFalse.statement: El viajero tendrá que pasar la noche en un hotel.
trueFalse.explanation: El agente encuentra un asiento en el vuelo de las ocho, así que el viajero llegará a tiempo a la reunión de la mañana siguiente.

teacherTips: Enseña antes la estructura condicional 'If there is… then I will…', una frase clave para resolver problemas de la vida real.
Después de escuchar, los estudiantes discuten por parejas: '¿Alguna vez perdiste un vuelo? ¿Qué hiciste?'.
Ampliación: los estudiantes hacen un role-play de queja en la recepción de un hotel o en una tienda usando las mismas estructuras educadas.
